```{r libararies, include = FALSE}
#general (from photosynthesis project, some might be unused)
library(lubridate)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyverse)
library(RColorBrewer)
```

```{r load data, include = FALSE}
pre_data <- read_csv("Data/TEMPEST_LeafSampleList_ISO_Ions_202605 - forR(SampleList).csv") |> 
  head(56) #kept returning 999 blank rows for some reason?
#i did cheat and manually add a plot column. seemed faster than trying to figure out the r verison
#alternative version: just delete a bunch of rows in excel
#mapping spreadsheet: its like a masterlist of metadata on stuff that can be used to do that for you

post_data_partial <- read_csv("Data/TEMPEST_LeafSampleList_ISO_Ions_202607_ForR_INCOMPLETE.csv") |> 
  head(54)

post_data <-  read_csv("Data/TEMPEST_LeafSampleList_ISO_Ions_202607_ForR.csv") |> 
  head(54) |> 
  select(!contains("..."))

#get mean and sd for each isotope grouped by species and plot
grouped_pre_data <- pre_data |>
  group_by(Species, Plot) |>
  filter(!is.na(Br)) |> 
  mutate(
    d13C_mean = mean(d13C), 
    d15N_mean = mean(d15N),
    Br_mean = mean(Br), 
    Cl_mean = mean(Cl),
    NO3_mean = mean(NO3),
    PO4_mean = mean(PO4),
    SO4_mean = mean(SO4),
    Br_sd = sd(Br), 
    Cl_sd = sd(Cl),
    NO3_sd = sd(NO3),
    PO4_sd = sd(PO4),
    SO4_sd = sd(SO4)
  )

grouped_post_data_partial <- post_data_partial |> 
  group_by(Species, Plot) |>
  mutate(
    d13C_mean = mean(d13C), 
    d15N_mean = mean(d15N))

grouped_post_data <- post_data |> 
  group_by(Species, Plot) |>
  filter(!is.na(Br))|> 
  mutate(
    d13C_mean = mean(d13C), 
    d15N_mean = mean(d15N),
    Br_mean = mean(Br), 
    Cl_mean = mean(Cl),
    NO3_mean = mean(NO3),
    PO4_mean = mean(PO4),
    SO4_mean = mean(SO4),
    Br_sd = sd(Br), 
    Cl_sd = sd(Cl),
    NO3_sd = sd(NO3),
    PO4_sd = sd(PO4),
    SO4_sd = sd(SO4))
 

```

*Pre-Campaign Iso*

```{r summarize ions pre: box plot, echo=FALSE}

####THIS IS PRE-CAMPAIGN DATA


#idea: box and whisker plots? (show range, which would be useful to know)
#can i cluster by plot but show by species? (yes! fill = does this)

#could be fun to color these fun and not with plots

#all appear mostly similar, minus a very wide range for saltwater litu
ggplot(grouped_pre_data, aes(x = Plot, fill = Species, y = Br)) +
  geom_boxplot() + labs(title = "Pre-Campaign 2026 Leaf Br", y = "Br (mg/kg dw)") +
  theme_bw()

#much higher in the saltwater plot, especially LITU! 
#control and fresh are all similar
#saltwater has a higher range, litu still is wayyyy higher
ggplot(grouped_pre_data, aes(x = Plot, fill = Species, y = Cl)) +
  geom_boxplot() + theme_bw() + 
  labs(title = "Pre-Campaign 2026 Leaf Cl", y = "Cl (mg/kg dw)") 

#not much difference across plots, it's more species-differences
#litu tends to be higher, fagr tends to be a but lower
ggplot(grouped_pre_data, aes(x = Plot, fill = Species, y = NO3)) +
  geom_boxplot() + theme_bw() + labs(title = "Pre-Campaign 2026 Leaf NO3", y = "NO3 (mg/kg dw)")

#a bit of variation again, but mostly contained to litu
#beech runs mostly similar, acru is higher in freshwater and more in saltwater
#litu is similar control fresh but much higher salt
ggplot(grouped_pre_data, aes(x = Plot, fill = Species, y = PO4)) +
  geom_boxplot() + theme_bw() + labs(title = "Pre-Campaign 2026 Leaf PO4", y = "PO4 (mg/kg dw)")

#nothing of note
ggplot(grouped_pre_data, aes(x = Plot, fill = Species, y = SO4)) +
  geom_boxplot() + theme_bw() +  labs(title = "Pre-Campaign 2026 Leaf SO4", y = "SO4 (mg/kg dw)")
```

```{r mean + sd, echo = FALSE}
table_data_pre <- read_csv("Data/Veg Campaign Leaf Iso Mean SD (CSV-Friendly) 202605.csv") |> 
  head(9)

# ggplot(table_data, aes(fill = Plot, y = Cl_mean, identity = Species)) +
#   geom_bar() + theme_bw()


# ggplot(table_data, aes(x = Plot, y= Cl_mean, fill = Species)) + 
#   geom_bar(stat = "identity")


long_pre <- table_data_pre %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -c(Plot, Species),
    names_to = c("Analyte", ".value"),
    names_pattern = "^([A-Za-z0-9]+)_(mean|sd)$"
  ) |> 
  filter(!is.na(Analyte))
 
 
ggplot(long_pre, aes(x = Species, y = mean, fill = Analyte)) +
  geom_col(position = "stack") +
  facet_wrap(~ Plot) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set1") + #not my fave color pallette but not ugly yellow so
  labs(
    title = "Pre-Campaign Cumulative Analyte Concentrations by Species",
    x = "Species",
    y = "Mean concentration (mg/kg dw)",
    fill = "Analyte"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() 



#breaking up the graph!
step1 <- long_pre |> 
  filter(Analyte == "Br")

ggplot(step1, aes(x = Species, y = mean, fill = Analyte)) +
  geom_col(position = "stack") +
  facet_wrap(~ Plot) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set1") + #not my fave color pallette but not ugly yellow so
  labs(
    title = "Pre-Campaign Cumulative Analyte Concentrations by Species",
    x = "Species",
    y = "Mean concentration (mg/kg dw)",
    fill = "Analyte"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() 

step2 <- long_pre |> 
  filter(Analyte == "Br" | Analyte == "Cl")
  

ggplot(step2, aes(x = Species, y = mean, fill = Analyte)) +
  geom_col(position = "stack") +
  facet_wrap(~ Plot) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set1") + #not my fave color pallette but not ugly yellow so
  labs(
    title = "Pre-Campaign Cumulative Analyte Concentrations by Species",
    x = "Species",
    y = "Mean concentration (mg/kg dw)",
    fill = "Analyte"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() 


step3 <- long_pre |> 
  filter(Analyte == "Br" | Analyte == "Cl" | Analyte == "NO3")

ggplot(step3, aes(x = Species, y = mean, fill = Analyte)) +
  geom_col(position = "stack") +
  facet_wrap(~ Plot) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set1") + #not my fave color pallette but not ugly yellow so
  labs(
    title = "Pre-Campaign Cumulative Analyte Concentrations by Species",
    x = "Species",
    y = "Mean concentration (mg/kg dw)",
    fill = "Analyte"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() 


step4 <- long_pre |> 
  filter(Analyte != "SO4")

ggplot(step4, aes(x = Species, y = mean, fill = Analyte)) +
  geom_col(position = "stack") +
  facet_wrap(~ Plot) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set1") + #not my fave color pallette but not ugly yellow so
  labs(
    title = "Pre-Campaign Cumulative Analyte Concentrations by Species",
    x = "Species",
    y = "Mean concentration (mg/kg dw)",
    fill = "Analyte"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() 


ggplot(long_pre, aes(x = Species, y = mean, fill = Analyte)) +
  geom_col(position = "stack") +
  facet_wrap(~ Plot) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set1") + #not my fave color pallette but not ugly yellow so
  labs(
    title = "Pre-Campaign Cumulative Analyte Concentrations by Species",
    x = "Species",
    y = "Mean concentration (mg/kg dw)",
    fill = "Analyte"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

*Compare Campaign Iso*
```{r pre v post, echo = FALSE}
pre_post_iso_diff <- 
  merge(x = pre_data, y = post_data, by = "Sapflux_ID", suffixes = c("Pre", "Post")) |> 
  filter(!is.na(BrPre)) |> 
  mutate(
    Plot = PlotPre,
    Species = SpeciesPre,
    Br_percent_change = ((BrPost - BrPre) / BrPre) * 100, # NOTE SOME OF THESE PRE = 0 SO THERE ARE /0 ERRORS
    Cl_percent_change = ((ClPost - ClPre) / ClPre) * 100,
    NO3_percent_change = ((NO3Post - NO3Pre) / NO3Pre) * 100,
    PO4_percent_change = ((PO4Post - PO4Pre) / PO4Pre) * 100, 
    SO4_percent_change = ((SO4Post - SO4Pre) / SO4Pre) * 100) |> 
  select(
    Sapflux_ID, Plot, Species, 
    BrPre, BrPost, ClPre, ClPost, NO3Pre, NO3Post, PO4Pre, PO4Post, SO4Pre, SO4Post,
    Br_percent_change, Cl_percent_change, NO3_percent_change, PO4_percent_change, SO4_percent_change) |> 
  group_by(Species, Plot) |> 
  mutate(
    Br_mean_pChange = mean(Br_percent_change),
    Cl_mean_pChange = mean(Cl_percent_change),
    NO3_mean_pChange = mean(NO3_percent_change),
    PO4_mean_pChange = mean(PO4_percent_change),
    SO4_mean_pChange = mean(SO4_percent_change)
  )


#box and whiskers to visualize per-species
ggplot(pre_post_iso_diff, aes(x = Plot, y = Br_percent_change, fill = Species)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "darkgrey") +
  geom_boxplot() + theme_bw() + 
  labs(title = "Veg Campaign Br % Change", y = "% Change Br", caption = "Note: LITU Control initial Br = 0, no # for % change") 

ggplot(pre_post_iso_diff, aes(x = Plot, y = Cl_percent_change, fill = Species)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "darkgrey") +
  geom_boxplot() + theme_bw() + 
  labs(title = "Veg Campaign Cl % Change", y = "% Change Cl") 

ggplot(pre_post_iso_diff, aes(x = Plot, y = NO3_percent_change, fill = Species)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "darkgrey") +
  geom_boxplot() + theme_bw() + 
  labs(title = "Veg Campaign NO3 % Change", y = "% Change NO3") 

ggplot(pre_post_iso_diff, aes(x = Plot, y = PO4_percent_change, fill = Species)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "darkgrey") +
  geom_boxplot() + theme_bw() + 
  labs(title = "Veg Campaign PO4 % Change", y = "% Change PO4") 

ggplot(pre_post_iso_diff, aes(x = Plot, y = SO4_percent_change, fill = Species)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "darkgrey") +
  geom_boxplot() + theme_bw() + 
  labs(title = "Veg Campaign SO4 % Change", y = "% Change SO4") 




#bar charts
ggplot(pre_post_iso_diff |> filter_out((Species == "LITU" & Plot == "Control")), aes(x = Species, y = Br_mean_pChange, fill = Species)) + 
  geom_col(position = "identity") + 
  facet_wrap(~Plot) + theme_bw() + 
  labs(title = "Veg Campaign Mean Br % Change", y = "Mean % Change Br", caption = "Note: All LITU control initial Br = 0, so % change has been removed from this graph.") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0)
#THIS ONE NEEDS TO FILTER OUT THE INF ERROR !!!

ggplot(pre_post_iso_diff, aes(x = Species, y = Cl_mean_pChange, fill = Species)) + 
  geom_col(position = "identity") + 
  facet_wrap(~Plot) + theme_bw() + 
  labs(title = "Veg Campaign Mean Cl% Change", y = "Mean % Change Cl") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0)

ggplot(pre_post_iso_diff, aes(x = Species, y = NO3_mean_pChange, fill = Species)) + 
  geom_col(position = "identity") + 
  facet_wrap(~Plot) + theme_bw() + 
  labs(title = "Veg Campaign Mean NO3% Change", y = "Mean % Change NO3") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0)

ggplot(pre_post_iso_diff, aes(x = Species, y = PO4_mean_pChange, fill = Species)) + 
  geom_col(position = "identity") + 
  facet_wrap(~Plot) + theme_bw() + 
  labs(title = "Veg Campaign Mean PO4% Change", y = "Mean % Change PO4") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0)

ggplot(pre_post_iso_diff, aes(x = Species, y = SO4_mean_pChange, fill = Species)) + 
  geom_col(position = "identity") + 
  facet_wrap(~Plot) + theme_bw() + 
  labs(title = "Veg Campaign Mean SO4% Change", y = "Mean % Change SO4") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0)

```

*Carbon/Nitrogen*
#C, N work
```{r carbon nitrogen, echo = FALSE}

#dC13 notes: 
  #rubisco prefers to fix C12 from atmosphere
  #water stress = close stomata = stop atm exchange = using more C13 
  #so more water stress = higher C13
  #reference is a super high # so all are negative, lower magnitude = higher C13

#dN15 notes: 
  #baseline is atmospheric N15 concentration, not a sample
  #less straightforward than C13 (?) tells us about N fixation/mutualisms
  #still a little fuzzy on this

#how to graph?
  #might help to just see what it looks like with box and whisker and adjust accordingly

ggplot(grouped_pre_data, aes(x = Plot, y = d13C, fill = Species)) +
  geom_boxplot()  + theme_bw() + 
  labs(title = "Pre-Campaign 2026 Leaf d13C", y = "d13C") 

ggplot(grouped_pre_data, aes(x = Plot, y = d15N, fill = Species)) + 
  geom_boxplot()  + theme_bw() + 
  labs(title = "Pre-Campaign 2026 Leaf d15N", y = "d15N") 

ggplot(grouped_pre_data, aes(x = Plot, y = C_N_ratio, fill = Species))+ 
  geom_boxplot()  + theme_bw() + 
  labs(title = "Pre-Campaign 2026 Leaf C/N", y = "C/N")

ggplot(grouped_post_data_partial, aes(x = Plot, y = d15N, fill = Species)) +

ggplot(grouped_post_data_partial, aes(x = Plot, y = C_N_ratio, fill = Species))+

#this is an idea/proof of concept thing, not super tied to any of it
#differences
pre_post_CN_diff <- 
  merge(x = pre_data, y = post_data_partial, by = "Sapflux_ID", suffixes = c("Pre", "Post")) |> 
  filter(!is.na(d13CPre)) |> 
  mutate(
    Plot = PlotPre,
    Species = SpeciesPre,
    d13C_percent_change = ((d13CPost - d13CPre) / d13CPre) * 100, # % change = new - old / old *100
    d15N_percent_change = ((d15NPost - d15NPre) / d15NPre) * 100,
    CN_percent_change = ((C_N_ratioPost - C_N_ratioPre) / C_N_ratioPre) * 100) |> 
  select(
    Sapflux_ID, Plot, Species, 
    d13CPre, d13CPost, d15NPre, d15NPost, C_N_ratioPre, C_N_ratioPost,
    d13C_percent_change, d15N_percent_change, CN_percent_change ) |> 
  group_by(Species, Plot) |> 
  mutate(
    d13C_mean_pChange = mean(d13C_percent_change),
    d15N_mean_pChange = mean(d15N_percent_change),
    CN_mean_pChange = mean(CN_percent_change)
  )



#seemed like a possibility for looking at, but not sure how to interpret
ggplot(pre_post_CN_diff, aes(x = Plot, y = d13C_percent_change, fill = Species)) +

  labs(title = "Veg Campaign d13C % Change", y = "% Change d13C")
```
